To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alkaliphilic bacteria do not possess special structures in the membrane that are required for their ability to function optimally at alkaline pH.

the cytoplasm of Bacillus firmis OF4 and Bacillius alcalophilus cells grown at pH 10 is indistinguishable from that of Bacillus subtilus BD99 cells grown at pH7, and that no special structures are associated with the cytoplasms or cytoplasmic or cell walls of these cells.

the cytoplasm membranes of Bacillus alcalophilius, Bacillus firmus, and Bacillus subtilus are indistinguishable and that the cytoplamsic membranes do not show any vesicles or other structures associated with the adaptation to growth at alkaliphilic pH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which bacteria adapt to the environment.
the molecular basis for growth at alkaline (pH 9.5) pH.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the adaptation of bacteria to extreme environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytoplasm of alkaliphilics is not different in structure from that of neutrophilics.
the alkaliphilicity of these bacilli is not associated with any unique membrane ultrastructural feature.

the alkaline pH-adapted cells have no special vesicular structures within or associated with their cytoplasmic or outer membranes, but do have intramembrane particles in the cytoplasmatic membrane which are probably associated with the flagella.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultrastructure of Bacillus species is remarkably similar, and that this similarity extends to both the cytoplasm and the cytoplasm-membrane interface.

the cytoplasm of the alkaliphile, Bacillus firmus, is indistinguishable from that of the neutrophile, Bacillus subtilus, except for a few minor differences, e.g., a few more ribosomes, and the absence of a cell wall.
there is no evidence of any specialized structures associated with the adaptation to growth at alkaliphilic conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no obvious structural differences between alkaliphilic and neutrophilic bacteria.
the alkaliphilicity of these organisms appears to be the result of a complex of adaptations that are not easily detected by electron microscopy.
, despite their ability to thrive in alkaline environments, the alkaliphillic Bacillus strains do not have any unique ultrastructural features.
